Genome scan of the rotated second stage

Source: R/scan.R
genome_scan.Rd

Tests every marker one at a time with the variance components held at their values from the model without a marker (the population parameters previously determined approximation): the ratio of the residual to the genetic variance is fixed, the residual scale is re-estimated at each marker, and the marker effect is tested by a t statistic on \(n - p - 1\) degrees of freedom. Under the rotation every marker column is rotated with the same matrix as the means, so the scan is the ordinary mixed-model GWAS of the rotated data. The two approximate schemes are offered for comparison: inverse-variance weighting divides each mean by its own standard error and treats the estimation errors as uncorrelated; the unweighted analysis ignores the first-stage variance-covariance matrix altogether. Each scheme fits its own model without a marker.

Usage

genome_scan(
  x,
  markers,
  scheme = "rotated",
  alpha = 0.05,
  chunk_size = 5000,
  model = NULL,
  fit = c("free", "residual_one")
)

Arguments

x

a rotation object.

markers

numeric matrix of marker dosages (0, 1, 2), accessions in rows with the accession names as row names, markers in columns; complete.

scheme

the scheme or schemes to scan under: "rotated" (the default), "inverse_variance", "unweighted", or several of them.

alpha

the genome-wide level of the Bonferroni threshold, applied to the number of markers with a test.

chunk_size

markers per block of matrix products.

model

optionally an independent_effect object: the scan then runs under the rotated model with the independent effect, at its fitted variance components (scheme must be "rotated"). A warning is given when that model's free fit has the residual variance at the boundary of zero, where the model is the unweighted analysis.

fit

with model, which of its fits supplies the variance components held in the scan: the free fit ("free", the default) or the fit with the residual variance fixed at one ("residual_one").

Value

a data frame of class genome_scan with one row per marker and scheme: marker, scheme, maf, beta (the marker effect per dose), se, t, neglog10p and significant (above the Bonferroni threshold). A marker without variance has NA in the test columns. Attributes: fits, a data frame with one row per scheme (the genetic, independent and residual variances of the model without a marker, the ratio of residual to genetic variance, the boundary status, the genomic inflation factor of the scan, the numbers of markers tested and significant), threshold (in \(-\log_{10} p\)), alpha, n, p, df and model ("additive", "additive + independent effect" or "additive + independent effect, residual variance fixed at one").

Details

The residual variance is estimated in the scan under every scheme, also under the rotation, where its target is one; the test of the residual variance is a separate step (specification_test()). Markers close to the significance threshold can be refitted afterwards with the marker in the model and the residual variance fixed at one (refit_markers()). When the test finds the residual variance above one, the scan can be run under the model extended by an effect independent across accessions, from independent_effect(), through model; that model is defined under the rotation only, and its variance components are held at their fitted values in the same way, either from its free fit or, with fit = "residual_one", from its fit with the residual variance fixed at one. The paper adds the effect to the model when the test rejects but does not evaluate a scan under the extended model; the option is offered here so that the scan can follow the model the test led to.

Examples

ex <- rotationGWAS:::toy_trial(n = 40, n_markers = 60, seed = 2)
r <- rotation(ex$means, ex$Omega, ex$relationship, ex$covariates)
s <- genome_scan(r, ex$markers, scheme = c("rotated", "unweighted"))
summary(s)
#> Genome scan of 40 accessions, 3 fixed effects, 36 degrees of freedom per marker; Bonferroni threshold 3.079 in -log10 p at alpha 0.05
